summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes and a history of kidney transplant was admitted for fevers up to 102.4°F, nausea, fatigue, and mild abdominal pain. He had a PICC line for home micafungin therapy due to prior fungal peritonitis. Workup showed no growth in blood or urine cultures, a negative CMV viral load, and a chest X-ray without acute findings. Renal ultrasound revealed resolution of a prior perinephric fluid collection, leading to discontinuation of micafungin. The PICC line was removed, and the patient was treated with vancomycin for presumed line-associated bacteremia. After defervescing, he completed five days of inpatient vancomycin and was discharged on a two-day course of oral linezolid. Potassium remained elevated, so kayexalate was continued twice weekly, and calcium carbonate was held. He was stable on all chronic medications, including tacrolimus and insulin, and was discharged home with follow-up planned in transplant and infectious disease clinics.
